# Organizations

This area groups the institutional and organizational entities that structure, govern, and deliver healthcare in Denmark, specifically within the context of the national atrial fibrillation quality assurance programs. It encompasses clinical providers like hospitals and clinics, regional and municipal administrative bodies, and the national authorities, registries, and professional societies that define standards and manage data infrastructure. Together, these organizations form the comprehensive ecosystem responsible for benchmarking cardiovascular care, tracking clinical outcomes, and driving systemic quality improvement across the Danish healthcare system.

## Pages

- [[entities/organizations/clinics/index|Clinics]] — Specialized and regional healthcare clinics evaluated for their compliance with national atrial fibrillation quality indicators.
- [[entities/organizations/health-authorities/index|Health Authorities]] — National and regional public organizations overseeing clinical quality development, health data infrastructure, and registry administration.
- [[entities/organizations/health-data-infrastructure/index|Health Data Infrastructure]] — Data infrastructure and analytical organizations, including prescription registries and analytical units, that power healthcare quality assurance programs.
- [[entities/organizations/health-databases/index|Health Databases]] — National clinical quality databases used to monitor and improve healthcare treatment, including the primary registry for atrial fibrillation care.
- [[entities/organizations/health-infrastructure/index|Health Infrastructure]] — Organizations operating foundational data pipelines and technical systems, such as national laboratory data hubs, that underpin healthcare monitoring.
- [[entities/organizations/health-quality-infrastructure/index|Health Quality Infrastructure]] — Institutional bodies responsible for defining, monitoring, and reviewing the quality of care and establishing evidence-based standards.
- [[entities/organizations/health-registries/index|Health Registries]] — National health registries and clinical quality databases providing the standardized, population-based data required to calculate clinical quality indicators.
- [[entities/organizations/health-standards/index|Health Standards]] — Organizations and governing bodies, including multidisciplinary steering committees, responsible for establishing and maintaining clinical health standards.
- [[entities/organizations/healthcare-registries/index|Healthcare Registries]] — Local healthcare clusters across Denmark's regions that serve as the primary geographic units for monitoring and benchmarking atrial fibrillation care.
- [[entities/organizations/hospital-units/index|Hospital Units]] — Specific clinical or operational departments within larger hospital organizations explicitly named in source documents for their impact on data capture and quality reporting.
- [[entities/organizations/hospitals/index|Hospitals]] — Danish hospitals evaluated in national clinical quality databases for their performance against standardized indicators and severe outcome metrics.
- [[entities/organizations/medical-societies/index|Medical Societies]] — Professional medical societies and special interest groups providing clinical governance, standardizing quality metrics, and driving implementation initiatives.
- [[entities/organizations/municipalities/index|Municipalities]] — Danish municipalities evaluated for their decentralized role in healthcare quality development, specifically tracking local compliance with safety and prevention standards.
- [[entities/organizations/regions/index|Regions]] — Regional administrative bodies, geographic health regions, and national spatial authorities that structure and report on cardiovascular care outcomes.
